proposals.evidence: CDIAL 13932 svāsṛka explicitly records Shina savuo/savui and Lorimer sau/sauwūo for sister’s son/daughter. HKAT Gilgit savō/savoy matches that gendered family. Turner nevertheless says the forms more probably derive from *svāsu(k)a, a secondary u-stem formation; that alternative has no separate parent record here. The proposed link is therefore to the dictionary’s family entry with its remote-etymon qualification, not an unqualified derivation from svāsṛka.
